newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks recover on fund flows from Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks recover on fund flows from Brazil.

text.p: Mexican substantially moderated earlier falls to close almost flat on Friday and well above the landmark 5,000 point barrier.
Dealers and analysts said bargain-hunters prompted the rebound following a similar recovery on Wall Street and portfolio allocations shifting to Mexico from Brazil.
"I suspect there was some window-dressing, or at least some pre-weekend at the close itself. Still, a recovery was under way for most of the afternoon," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended down 0.8 point, or 0.02 percent, at 5,067.03.
A surge in U.S. long bond spurred investors to take profits from record gains chalked up on Thursday and pushed the IPC down as low as 4,981.85 in early trade.
"Two elements were at work today, profit-taking or consolidation and the long bond, but mainly the latter," said Feliz Boni. research head at ING-Barings in Mexico.
"The fall was cushioned because long bond yields are still relatively low and there were signs of funds transferring to Mexico from Brazil," he added.
The 30-Treasury bonds were up 67/32 to yield 6.46 percent in late dealing.

The Bovespa index of most active stocks traded in Sao Paulo dived 4.76 percent to close at 12,259. The Salomon Brothers brokerage announced it cut its recommended portfolio weighting for Brazil while raising Mexico.
Dealers said market heavyweights Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Grupo Carso were pace-setters for the bourse, both ending unchanged after recovering from profit-taking.
Telecomms firm Telmex ended at 21.60 pesos while conglomerate Carso closed at 62.40 pesos.
Dealers pointed to a strong performance by construction companies and some cement stocks.
The stocks gained on speculation a government scheme to restructure highway concession debts was imminent.
Construction firm Empresas ICA gained 70 centavos to 24.70 pesos, while cement maker Cemex climbed 1.00 peso to 40.20 pesos.
Trading volume was brisk at 159.1 million shares, even after allowing for one cross trade which accounted for 47 million shares.
On the broad market, slides outpaced gains by 45 to 50, out of 120 stocks traded in total.
